q-73987.name: Question 1
q-73987.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨1,1,1⟩+t⟨5,2,-4⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨2,-3,5⟩=36.
$$
q-73987.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨1+5t,1+2t,1-4t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1+5t,1+2t,1-4t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨2,-3,5⟩ & =36 \\ ⟨1+5t,1+2t,1-4t⟩\cdot ⟨2,-3,5⟩ & =36 \\ 2(1+5t)-3(1+2t)+5(1-4t) & =36 \\ 2+10t-3-6t+5-20t & =36 \\ -16t & =32 \\ t & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=-2$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨1+5(-2),1+2(-2),1-4(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-9,-3,9⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(-9,-3,9).$

q-108315.name: Question 2
q-108315.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨1,-3,4⟩+t⟨4,-2,1⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨-2,-3,2⟩=1.
$$
q-108315.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨1+4t,-3-2t,4+t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1+4t,-3-2t,4+t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-2,-3,2⟩ & =1 \\ ⟨1+4t,-3-2t,4+t⟩\cdot ⟨-2,-3,2⟩ & =1 \\ -2(1+4t)+(-3)(-3-2t)+2\cdot (4+t) & =1 \\ -2-8t+9+6t+8+2t & =1 \\ 15 & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation has no solution. Therefore, we conclude that the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ do not intersect.

q-33068.name: Question 3
q-33068.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨3,0,1⟩+t⟨2,2,1⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨2,-1,4⟩=4.
$$
q-33068.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨3+2t,2t,1+t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3+2t,2t,1+t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨2,-1,4⟩ & =4 \\ ⟨3+2t,2t,1+t⟩\cdot ⟨2,-1,4⟩ & =4 \\ 2(3+2t)-2t+4(1+t) & =4 \\ 6+4t-2t+4+4t & =4 \\ 6t & =-6 \\ t & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=-1$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨3+2(-1),2(-1),1+(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-2,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(1,-2,0).$

Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨-1,2,1⟩+t⟨3,0,2⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩=13.
$$
q-108308.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨-1+3t,2,1+2t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨-1+3t,2,1+2t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ & =13 \\ ⟨-1+3t,2,1+2t⟩\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ & =13 \\ 1(-1+3t)-2+2(1+2t) & =13 \\ -1+3t-2+2+4t & =13 \\ 7t & =14 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=2$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨-1+3(2),2,1+2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨5,2,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(5,2,5).$

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨5-5(5),3+2(5),-4+7(5)⟩ \\  & =⟨-20,13,31⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(-20,13,31).$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨3+5(-3),1+2(-3),-4+3(-3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-12,-5,-13⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(-12,-5,-13).$

Finally, to get the position vector p of the intersection point P, we substitute t=2 into the equation of the line:

p=⟨1+2(2),−2+2,1+3(2)⟩=⟨5,0,7⟩.

So, we get P(5,0,7).
